messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected — hosted-runtime pool-7 KV cache memory growth > 80% across nodes (OOM risk). Alert ID INC-1755002469
maya: seeing spike in kv_map sizes, looks tied to very long concatenated prompts from a small subset of sessions
dan: @maya can you paste an example request? might be the same doc-assembly job we saw last week
maya: example payload snippet: ```{\n  \"session_id\": \"s-9a8\",\n  \"prompt_bytes\": 189432,\n  \"segments\": 48,\n  \"pattern\": \"<doc>...<doc>...<doc>\"\n}```
sam: oncall ack, taking ownership
sam: paging eng-runtime and eng-ml teams, @dan @rick please triage now
rick: looking at pool-7, starting a canary hotfix: reduce kv prefetch depth from 12 -> 4 on 2 nodes
lena: also enabling soft eviction policy and session cap on the pool (session_cap=1) to limit multi-doc sessions
cs-tilly: tagging CS: customers impacted: docs-assembler (high), notebook-inc (medium) — preparing comms if latency persists
maya: correlation: memory climbs rapidly when continuous-batching window > 8k tokens per batch; that grew after yesterday's batch-window tuning deploy
dan: can confirm, last deploy increased batch_window_ms and allowed longer prefix batching, exposing long-prefix cases
rick: reverting the batch-window tuning on canary now (rollback commit 3f5a2)
ops-bot: rollback deploy to pool-7 canary succeeded (deploy id: d-1755002475)
sam: @dan @rick please monitor kv_map_count, kv_heap_bytes, and OOM counts; alert if any node > 90%
dan: initial metric: after prefetch cut and rollback, memory growth rate dropped ~70% in 30s
rick: recommend temporary API Gateway guard: reject prompts > 200k bytes with 429 until batching heuristics patched
lena: applying gateway rule now: `max_prompt_bytes=200000` (soft 429) — rollout to hosted ingress in 2m
cs-tilly: letting impacted customers know to chunk uploads; offering guidance for streaming inputs
maya: running live evict script on survivors to speed reclaim (async evictions) — will log progress
dan: KV eviction backlog clearing, reclaim estimated ~20-40s per heavy session
rick: checking for any OOMs — none reported post rollback so far
sam: collating customer impact: latency spike and a few throttled requests. No data loss or session corruption reported
ops-bot: monitoring checks green after 8m steady-state on canary
lena: taking oncall handoff for night monitoring — @sam handing off; I'll keep trace alerts and set a 4h watch
sam: handing off, all oncall notes in the incident doc linked in #eng-oncall \nmaya: preliminary root cause: batch-window tuning increased allowed continuous-batch prefix length which allowed pathological long-prefix sessions to explode kv cache; also missing a prefetch circuit-breaker for extreme prompt lengths
rick: follow-ups: revert is live, API guard in place, schedule hotfix to introduce prefetch cap + batching heuristic update (ENG-4892)
cs-tilly: sent customer-facing note to affected accounts, asking them to reduce single-payload size; offer workaround: chunking or short-lived sessions
sam: severity -> P2, partial customer impact (throughput/latency). No SLA breaches at this time
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — pool-7 memory stabilized, incident duration 00:23:51, incident id INC-1755002469
maya: filing postmortem and linking logs + traces (PM: ENG-4892)
cs-tilly: drafting follow-up comms for tomorrow morning, will include mitigation steps
lena: taking overnight watch, will escalate immediately on any regressions
sam: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
